A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DS4D work, with matching authors, core components and main experiments. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 ends with references; v3 includes supplementary material in Sections 7–13.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-to-4D comparisons, component ablations and real-scene experiments in Tables 1–3 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports input-quality robustness results and decoupling runtimes in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The core DSFD/TSSF procedure is retained, but v1 explicitly averages the two reference-conditioned feature branches in Section 3.3 and Figure 3. v3 removes that operation from both descriptions without specifying the replacement combination. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a procedural change or simplified exposition. Newly detailed losses and real-scene integration are presented as documentation of existing experiments.

E1.justification: The main datasets and tasks are retained. v3 additionally evaluates inconsistent or deformed ImageDream-generated multi-view inputs in Section 12.1 and explicitly reports Stable Video Diffusion-generated input videos in Section 11. These extend input conditions within the existing video-to-4D task.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set and real-scene 4D-GS baseline remain unchanged. Table 5 newly evaluates direct frame-by-frame decoupling against the proposed reference-selection approach. ImageDream supplies degraded inputs rather than serving as a competing 4D method.

E3.justification: v3 adds a protocol selecting inconsistent or deformed ImageDream outputs for robustness testing and a runtime comparison using a 30-frame video on an NVIDIA 3090. The existing DS4D schedule remains 1,000 plus 6,000 iterations, with unchanged main metrics. Newly specified Neu3D settings are disclosures, not evidence of revised experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Table 2 ablations, v3 adds input-quality robustness testing, direct-decoupling runtime analysis, point-initialization visualization, and additional DSFD/TSSF heatmaps and GA-versus-DA cases in Sections 12.1–12.7. These substantially extend analysis of robustness, efficiency and component behavior. The LPIPS ablation discussion refers to an existing result rather than a new ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 updates L4GM's Consistent4D scores: CLIP 0.9132 to 0.9158, LPIPS 0.1587 to 0.1497, FVD 1360.0434 to 898.0604, and FID-VID 40.2446 to 31.4996, without explaining the update. DS4D's main scores and Tables 2–3 remain unchanged. v3 adds degraded-input results, runtime measurements of 118.326 versus 8.241 ms for direct versus proposed decoupling, and additional qualitative results.

T1.justification: Section 8 newly formalizes the real/pseudo-view SDS decomposition and weighted overall objective, including reconstruction, mask and LPIPS terms, in Equations 6–7. v1 describes the loss families verbally. This is limited mathematical formalization; Equation 1's rewritten projection is algebraically equivalent, and no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The first contribution changes from proposing a novel framework to explicitly claiming, to the authors' knowledge, the first framework decoupling dynamic-static frame information along temporal-spatial axes for 4D generation. The principal performance, component and real-scene applicability claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly lists dependence on pseudo multi-view image quality as a limitation. v3 removes this caveat and concludes in Section 12.1 that input quality has little influence, attributing robustness to DINOv2 features and feature-level decoupling. This materially changes the stated applicability boundary. v3 also expands reference-selection and real-scene comparison rationales; the high-resolution limitation remains in Section 13.

D1.justification: Sections 8–11 disclose loss composition, the VGG LPIPS backbone, camera settings, Neu3D train/evaluation allocation, and real-scene implementation details including TSSF-GA, SfM initialization, learning rates, batch size and 14,000 iterations. These substantially improve documentation of existing experiments. The original DS4D training schedule is relocated unchanged, while explicit DSFD branch averaging disappears. Code availability remains a future promise.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for VGG, Stable Video Diffusion and ImageDream, while removing the visual-foundation-model comparison supported by references to Probing the 3D Awareness of Visual Foundation Models, latent diffusion and CLIP. The related-work framework largely remains, alongside the stronger first-method positioning in the introduction.

P1.justification: Reference selection, DSFD decomposition and GA/DA fusion explanations undergo substantial rewriting. Training and dataset descriptions are redistributed into dedicated supplementary sections, and limitations move from Section 6 to Section 13. Some revised cross-references are incorrect, including Section 3.3 pointing to Figure 13 for the architecture.

P2.justification: Tables 4–5 and Figures 10–18 substantially expand the visual presentation with robustness comparisons, timing, initialization, feature visualizations and generation examples. Figure 3 is redrawn without the averaging stage, and Figure 5 updates L4GM imagery. Most original figures and table structures remain, with some relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 make previously unquantified robustness and efficiency arguments assessable, while Sections 8–11 improve documentation of losses, data and real-scene experiments. These useful gains are partly offset by removing the input-quality caveat on the basis of a limited selected-input test, losing explicit DSFD branch-combination detail, and introducing incorrect figure references. The net improvement is meaningful but limited.
